facts.text: I have pain in my lower back.
It came on gradually, about seven months ago.
It has slowly been getting worse.
It spreads down into my legs.

facts.item: low back pain: what makes it worse
facts.text: Walking makes it worse.

facts.item: low back pain: what makes it better
facts.text: Resting makes it better.
I get short of breath when I exert myself.
I've been feeling tired.
I've been having palpitations; I can feel my heart beating.

facts.item: when the breathlessness, tiredness and palpitations started
facts.text: The breathlessness, tiredness and palpitations started about four months ago.
I've lost weight.
I've been having fevers.
I've been feeling generally unwell.
I have to strain to pass urine.
I need to pass urine more often than usual.
It hurts when I pass urine.
I haven't had any injury.
I don't have a cough.
I haven't had any stomach or bowel problems.
I've never smoked.
I don't drink alcohol.
I'm from Namibia.
My doctor sent me here because I was found to be anemic.
I was also told my platelet count is low.
My right shoulder is swollen.
I can't move my right shoulder as far as I should.

gold.reasoning: 1. The absence of skull or jaw lesions argued against multiple myeloma—“he had no lytic lesions in the skull bones or mandible.” 2. Negative serum protein electrophoresis and absence of Bence Jones proteins further excluded multiple myeloma—“serum electrophoresis was negative for M-protein and there were no Bence Jones proteins in the urine.”

x009: The source calls liver function normal but reports an elevated alkaline phosphatase; both are kept as stated (ALP grouped with the liver panel).
x010: 'Elevated' read as applying to both alkaline phosphatase and LDH in s011.

leakage.reason: Result names the organ (hard nodular prostate); points to prostate cancer without naming it. Bedside finding kept as reported.
Test name contains 'prostate' (clinical name of the test); PSA >100 ng/mL strongly points to the diagnosis (selection leakage: test_result).

source_issues: Liver function tests are reported normal alongside an elevated alkaline phosphatase (509 IU/L); the source does not reconcile them (likely bone origin).
s012 holds two sentences (renal and liver tests; protein electrophoresis and Bence Jones proteins).
notes: Index visit: the referral evaluation (admission) for anemia, thrombocytopenia and back pain (s001); s002–s005 give the history leading up to it, and all examination and test results are from this workup.
f019 is a system-level blanket denial ('no gastrointestinal symptoms'); it answers a general question about stomach or bowel problems, not a specific GI symptom.
f010 is a standalone onset fact because the four-month onset applies to three symptoms (breathlessness, tiredness, palpitations); s004 symptoms have no stated onset.
Signs the patient can notice (swollen, stiff right shoulder) are facts and also stay in the examination finding; pallor and wasting stay in the examination (weight loss is a fact).
x004 and x015 keep 'prostate' in their names (digital rectal / prostate examination, prostate-specific antigen) because the tests are named that way clinically; both are listed in qc.leakage.
x008 groups calcium with the renal function tests (metabolic panel); x009 groups alkaline phosphatase with the liver function tests.
